The book of the debt (less than the spring, a good deal more than nothing) and the day's price written under it in two lines; Hale's question, what the captain of the Ninth is worth to the Holloway, answered with a joke and not answered (the refusal kept quiet); the packet in salt for the river mill, carried and not opened ('As usual'). note: Chapter 5's climax, Hard-won (82): the arc's shape (a night in a barn on the tarn, away before the dawn bell, Ash giving them away once and forgiven) with Rae's choice as the hinge: out of her uncle's inn before light so he has nothing to not-see, the fold on the north shore, herself at the reading with her village. The cost: the summer written against her unsigned (Hale: 'signed or not; the book's open'), the first time she drove out of his yard with her bell stopped. Dice: insight on Hale partial (he will not sell them today, for Rae; the book unread; he saw Darrow look); resolve partial (his name read across the water, hands on the wall; the cost: watching Rae questioned and staying; holding Hollis); finesse success (out before the bell, clean). Ash barked at the grey cloaks and the mill carter whose boy was pulled from the axle claimed her. The levy sergeant did not return; Oswin gone; the lone rider (thread 23) unseen. Rae's cart is now known to the grey cloaks by name as working. Thread 18: Hale's book tells only.
next_must_know: The climax choice is open: east by the river road (road_east; Rae approves) or north by the mill tracks (Hollis approves; the default). Two scenes into chapter 6, then the default. The grey cloaks asked at the mill. Rae's summer is written against her in Hale's book, unsigned.
